text:
sophie (support): Hey — customer reporting intermittent 500s and very high latency for their /v1/generate calls around 2025-03-12T18:22:15Z. They gave a request_id: req_9a7b3c2f. Repro steps attached, can ops pull server logs for that reqid and check if it hit fallback model or was rate-limited?

sophie (support): curl they used (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -d '{"model": "redwood-7b", "input": "summarize ...", "max_tokens": 512}'
```

jamal (eng-oncall): pinging eng-oncall. Do you have exact client timestamp and region? request_id alone is fine but timestamp helps narrow shards.

sophie (support): customer timezone UTC, said event at 2025-03-12T18:22:15Z (approx). Region us-west-2. Also saw "latency: 8.2s" in their client logs.

alena (eng-sre): I can look but note retention policy: hot indices only keep 14 days, cold storage up to 90 days. If event is older than 14 days it may be in cold tier which needs an export job. Your timestamp is within 14 days — should be in hot indices. I'll run a KQL query first.

alena (eng-sre): KQL to run in Kibana:
```
request_id.keyword: \"req_9a7b3c2f\" AND service:\"edge-api\" AND @timestamp:[\"2025-03-12T18:20:00.000Z\" TO \"2025-03-12T18:25:00.000Z\"]
```
Or Splunk:
```
index=redwood_edge request_id=\"req_9a7b3c2f\" earliest=\"03/12/2025:18:20:00\" latest=\"03/12/2025:18:25:00\"
```

alena (eng-sre): If nothing shows, try searching trace_id or parent_request_id; client SDKs sometimes send a different internal request_id. Also sample grep on pod logs:
```
kubectl logs -n edge -l app=edge-api --since=30m | grep 'req_9a7b3c2f'
```

sophie (support): running the grep now — customer says they see a different trace in their headers: x-trace-id: trace-0x5f8c. Adding that in case.

mike (backend): noted — sometimes embedded proxies rewrite req ids. I'll check upstream proxies and gateway logs.

alena (eng-sre): FYI if it is in cold storage I'll open an export job. Command (ops-only):
```
POST /internal/logs/export
{ "ids": ["req_9a7b3c2f"], "time_range": ["2025-03-12T18:20:00Z","2025-03-12T18:25:00Z"], "destination": "s3://redwood-support-exports/2025/03/12/" }
```
Expect ~15–45m for cold fetch.

infra-export-bot: Started export job job_id=exp-20250312-2245 for req_9a7b3c2f — status: queued. Link: https://internal.redwood.ai/ops/exports/exp-20250312-2245

sophie (support): thanks. Can you also advise customer on a curl that produces richer client headers for debugging?

alena (eng-sre): sure — ask them to run:
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -H 'X-Client-Time: 2025-03-12T18:22:15Z' \n -H 'X-Trace-Id: trace-0x5f8c' \n -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"test","max_tokens":10}' -o /tmp/resp.json -D /tmp/headers.txt
```
Then attach headers.txt and resp.json to the support ticket.

jamal (eng-oncall): if export finds no logs, escalate to infra for storage reindex + set a retention exception. Tag: #support-escalation.

sophie (support): copy — I'll tell customer and attach export link when ready. :thumbsup: 

infra-export-bot: export job exp-20250312-2245 completed. 1 file(s) at s3://redwood-support-exports/2025/03/12/exp-20250312-2245.tar.gz — sending to support thread.

sophie (support): received archive and scanned — found an upstream 502 from service upstream-auth at 18:22:15.217Z, plus a burst of 5xxs from model-proxy at 18:22:15-18:22:17. Sending to backend for root cause.

mike (backend): taking a look — starting pod log collection for model-proxy around that window. Will report back with a repro if I find request flow anomaly.

sophie (support): thanks all. Opening a follow-up ticket to propose increasing hot retention for this customer for 30 days while we complete RCA. ticket: SUP-4521.
